name: Refugee/Asylum Status

requirements.blocker_text: Thailand is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention or its 1967 Protocol and has no domestic legal framework defining or protecting refugee or asylum-seeker status. Thailand continues to operate under the 1979 Immigration Act, which treats asylum-seekers and refugees as illegal migrants subject to arrest, detention, and deportation regardless of any UNHCR documentation they hold. UNHCR is permitted a role in registration and refugee status determination, particularly for the roughly 90,000+ protracted refugees (predominantly Karen and other ethnic groups from Myanmar) held in camps along the Thailand-Myanmar border, and for a smaller population of self-settled 'urban refugees' in Bangkok, but this UNHCR determination confers no Thai government-recognised legal status.

sources.title: Human Rights Watch -- Thailand: Implement Commitments to Protect Refugee Rights, confirming non-signatory status to the 1951 Convention and 1967 Protocol and reporting approximately 102,000 refugees hosted, predominantly protracted Myanmar-border camp populations plus urban refugees in Bangkok

European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations (ECHO, EU intergovernmental body) -- Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia, confirming all three are non-signatories with no national legal protection mechanisms and describing them as illegal migrants under domestic law

notes: Uses the same 'never existed, not closed' convention established for the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, and Malaysia elsewhere in this dataset (closed_date: null, superseded_by: null). Thailand is the fifth confirmed case of this pattern in this dataset, and the third in maritime Southeast Asia specifically alongside Malaysia and Singapore -- the EU's own humanitarian-aid agency groups Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia together explicitly as a regional bloc sharing this same non-signatory, no-domestic-framework characteristic, reinforcing that this is a genuine regional pattern rather than three unrelated coincidences. Thailand's case carries a scale and duration dimension worth surfacing clearly: the Thailand-Myanmar border refugee camps have operated for multiple decades (some Karen refugee families have now been born and raised across two generations inside these camps, per multiple sources consulted in broader research for this build though not independently re-verified for this specific citation), making Thailand's 'never existed' formal-system gap one of the longest-running and largest-scale in this dataset by affected population, alongside the UAE and Saudi Arabia's much smaller comparable populations. h2_closed_notice-equivalent modeling: no_system_notice is hard:false for the same reason used throughout this dataset's other 'never existed' cases -- there is no test to fail, only a structural notice that no application process exists to follow.
